gap: No result ChatGPT got names the carriers behind SPYPOINT's dual SIM. Game & Fish lists the FLEX-M's two SIMs as AT&T and Verizon, so the free 100-photo plan only helps where one of those two networks reaches the stand. ChatGPT's results also left out SPYPOINT's own note that the Free plan is 'Not available on FLEX-RANGE'.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. ChatGPT's cited spypoint.com FLEX-M page says only 'all major cellular networks'. The SPYPOINT blog post (id=259) does not mention SIMs or carriers. Trailcamspecs says outright that it does not cover SIMs, carriers, solar or firmware. Cam & Canopy calls the FLEX-M 'single-SIM', which contradicts SPYPOINT's own page saying it is dual-SIM, and gives no carrier names. Outdoor Life only says the FLEX-M2 'Connects to multiple networks'. None of them names AT&T and Verizon or lists the FLEX-M's power pairings (8 AA, LIT-22 pack or a 12 V input). The FLEX-RANGE exclusion is printed on the cited SPYPOINT page, but ChatGPT's answer did not pass it on.
decides: It confirms that the SPYPOINT FLEX-M or FLEX-M2 is the right pick for a camera with no subscription, but adds a condition: check AT&T or Verizon coverage at the camera site before buying. Sources disagree on T-Mobile, so a T-Mobile-only area is a risk. The shopper also shouldn't pick the satellite FLEX-RANGE expecting the free tier. Where neither carrier reaches, the honest answer is an option with no plan at all, such as GardePro's long-range Wi-Fi Link system, which Dealectric already lists.
